deviations: Cargo's CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name> env var (both env! at compile time and std::env::var at runtime) is only set for a crate's OWN [[bin]] target, never for a dev-dependency's binary -- confirmed empirically. tests/pretooluse_hook_fixtures.rs instead resolves the built enforcer binary via std::env::current_exe() plus two .parent() calls (both crates' outputs land in the same shared target/<profile>/ dir). Recorded in memory/streams/c04.ndjson (mem-c04-0002) for future packs needing the same pattern.

enforcer coordination (and enforcer install/plan/proof) are unwired stubs in the compiled enforcer binary today (crates/enforcer-cli/src/main.rs dispatch() prints an internal-error placeholder for each) -- the workpack's 'enforcer check/scan + coordination guard' phrasing is honored via enforcer check (the one real, working entry point); the coordination-guard leg of the invocation is architecturally reserved (HOOK_ARGS/PreToolUseHookConfig do not hardcode a nonexistent CLI verb) rather than faked, and will compose automatically once arc-16's coordination guard CLI surface lands.

The emitted hook's argv carries a --hook-mode=pretooluse marker not read by today's enforcer check grammar (reserved for a future stdin-JSON hook-payload mode); until then the hook degrades to a plain `enforcer check <path>` invocation, which is what this pack's tests exercise end-to-end.

On Windows, `cargo test -p enforcer-install`'s compiled test binary name (enforcer_install-<hash>.exe) trips a UAC elevation heuristic (os error 740) unrelated to real permissions; __COMPAT_LAYER=RunAsInvoker in the shell env resolves it. Recorded in memory/streams/c04.ndjson (mem-c04-0001).
